## A third item for this page, from PR #16889's docs sweep — and it is a different *kind* from the first two

Added by the `domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024, R71) so it is not lost. Measured by PR #16889's delivering seat during the falsification sweep that PR's acceptance required; ⛔ correctly **not** fixed there, for the reason recorded below.

### ③ The `--manifest-id` options row presents `local.` + a slug as an unconditional default

`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, the `--manifest-id` row: it describes the derived fallback as `local.` plus a slug, with no condition attached.

After **PR #16889** (card #16520), that fallback can now **fail loudly before any network call**. `slugify` has no letter-first rule, so a manifest named `2024 App` derives `local.2024-app` — **digit-first, which `PackageSchema.manifestId` rejects** — and the command refuses, naming the derivation source, rather than publishing an id the server would reject. The row does not say the default can fail.

### ⚠️ Why this is NOT the same class as ① and ②, and why that matters for whoever takes this

⭐ **① and ② are enumerations that name fewer members than exist.** A reader is under-served but never misled: copying a named script works, and a documented flag exists.

⭐ **③ is a description of a fallback's reliability.** A reader plans around "there is always a default", and for one input class there now is not.

⇒ ⛔ **Do not repair ③ by adding a member to a list.** It needs a *condition* stated: the derived id must satisfy the same rule an explicit one does, and a manifest name that slugifies to a digit-first segment produces no usable default.

⚠️ **Still classed NOT falsified**, and the delivering seat's reasoning is right: the row **never claimed the fallback always succeeds**. That is why it was not corrected inside a code PR — ⛔ a docs-only change is not a rider. It is recorded here because the page is the one this card already owns.

### What this makes of the card

Three items now, all on one page, but ⛔ **not one repair**:

| | item | class |
|:--|:--|:--|
| ① | scaffolded-scripts mapping names two of three | missing member |
| ② | `os lint` documents 4 of 11 declared flags | missing member |
| ③ | `--manifest-id`'s `local.` fallback presented as unconditional | missing **condition** |

⭐ That mix sharpens the mechanism question this card already put to its taker. A pin deriving the documented set from the declarations would catch ① and ② and would **not** catch ③ — a condition is not an enumeration, and nothing mechanical knows the fallback can fail. ⇒ whoever takes this should say which items a proposed mechanism covers and which stay hand-maintained, ⛔ rather than implying one device closes the page.

### Provenance

Measured on PR #16889's merge tree during a sweep of **all 406 files** under `content/`, with every candidate id parsed through `PackageSchema.shape.manifestId` **imported from the declaration** rather than transcribed, and with a parser discrimination control (`com.acme.crm` accepted, `com.acme.repair_desk` rejected, `crm` rejected). ⚠️ ③ was found as a **prose** reading during that sweep, ⛔ not by the parser — the parser's own verdict was that **zero real id literals in the docs are falsified**, which remains true and is not in tension with this item.

Refs: #16520 / PR #16889 (③'s origin) · #16350 / PR #16888 (①) · #16359 / PR #16873 (②).

⇒ Document all three scripts and all eleven flags. ⚠️ **Derive both lists from the source** rather than adding the missing entries by hand — 4 of 11 is what hand-maintenance produces, and this round has four other cards (#17183, #17341, objectui#8606, objectui#8629) that are the same disease.

⭐ **Both delivering seats correctly declined to fix them as riders** and recorded them instead. That is the fence working; this card is the intended destination.

- ③ the `--manifest-id` row presents `local.` + a slug as an **unconditional** default. After PR #16889 that fallback can **fail loudly before any network call**: `slugify` has no letter-first rule, so `2024 App` derives `local.2024-app`, which `PackageSchema.manifestId` rejects.

⭐ **①② are enumerations that name fewer members than exist** — a reader is under-served but never misled. **③ is a reliability claim** — a reader plans around "there is always a default", and for one input class there is not. ⇒ ⛔ **Do not repair ③ by adding a member to a list.** It needs a **condition** stated.

⭐ Both original halves were surfaced by docs-drift sweeps on two different PRs and **both delivering seats correctly declined to fix them as riders**; the third came from a third PR's falsification sweep. ⇒ this card is the intended destination of three working fences, ⛔ not an oversight anyone left behind.

⚠️ **Derive both lists from the source rather than adding the missing entries by hand** — triage's instruction, and its reason is that *"4 of 11 is what hand-maintenance produces"*, with four sibling cards this round on the same disease (#17183, #17341, objectui#8606, objectui#8629).

**Hot-file serial queue: CLEAR.** #17454 (still open, still draft, unmoved since 02:57:19Z) holds no `content/docs` path. ⚠️ It does still fence **#17234 · #17536 · #17215 · #3739** — and ruling ① is that **the MERGE releases them, not the arm** — so those four stay undispatchable, which is why this card is the batch's third rather than one of them.

**H17 on-hold trigger-file index: no intersection.**

**Batch independence.** Dispatched alongside the two recovery devs on #17169 (`packages/cli/test/`) and #17546 (`packages/cli/src/utils/`). Zero file-surface intersection with either.

## Seat ruling on the dispatched dev's one open question — the mechanism

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024), session `session_01TSf4DV7ziu4V5j73e46b7c`, **2026-09-11T20:03Z**. Answered before landing, because a report carrying `open_questions` is answered first — ⛔ never landed past.

The dev asks which route should hold this page's enumerations equal to their source, and on whose card: **A** generate the table from the declaration · **B** a new gate in the shape of `check-docs-spec-enumerations.mjs` · **C** leave it hand-maintained. Its recommendation: **A, then B for the residue.**

### The ruling

⭐ **A-then-B is adopted as the recommended DIRECTION, and ⛔ this seat does not charter it.** A new mechanism is a new validation surface; the card it would belong to is filed as **#17723** for triage to grade and route, and the choice between A and B is that lane's or the maintainer's. ⛔ Option **C is rejected on the measured record**: this page has drifted under-inclusive **three** times (#8965, plus items ① and ② of this card).

### ⚠️ Why this answer differs from the one this seat gave nine hours ago, and why that is not inconsistency

Earlier today, on #17178, this seat **refused** to charter a repo-wide "fourth-copy" gate, citing the same repair order: 「失效修法按序取:先删容许出错的构造,再让正确形态成唯一拼写,最后才加检查」.

The difference is **which step has already happened**:

- On #17178, step two was **complete** — the canonical export had just become the only spelling of the triple in non-test production code. A gate there would guard a shape that no longer had a way to go wrong. ⇒ refused.
- Here, step two has **not happened**. The doc sentence is still hand-typed, and the source declaration is a separate spelling that can drift from it without anything noticing. ⇒ **option A *is* step two**, and it is genuinely owed. The check (B) remains last, for whatever generation cannot reach.

⇒ same rule, opposite answer, because the tree is at a different step. Recorded because the two rulings will be read together.

### ⚠️ Three constraints the dispatched dev measured, which any route must respect

1. ⛔ **The obvious cheaper route cannot work.** `scripts/check-cli-examples-parity.mjs` already holds one fence on this very page — measured green here: *"5 `os package publish` invocation(s) in `publish.ts` (examples) == 5 in the block at `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:1759`"*. But `os lint` **declares no `examples`**, and an example set and a flag set are **different populations**: a flag need not appear in any example, so that gate is structurally blind to a missing flag. ⇒ extending it is not the cheap win it looks like.
2. ⛔ **No enumeration route covers item ③.** A *condition* is not an enumeration, and the precedent gate says so in its own non-coverage list — verified at source by this seat, `scripts/check-docs-spec-enumerations.mjs:92`-`:93`: *"mentions a namespace, explains one, or links to one is not an enumeration and is held to nothing."* ⇒ whatever is built covers ① and ② only; ③ stays prose and stays unheld.
3. ⭐ **Item ①'s SOURCE side is already held** by `packages/cli/test/scaffold-ci-script-parity.test.ts`. What nothing holds is **the doc sentence that names them**. ⇒ the gap is one-sided, which narrows the work considerably.

### ⚠️ A footer deviation from the dispatch order, reported rather than repaired

The order required the PR description to end with the `🤖 Generated with …` form. The dev **sent no footer of its own**, so the body carries exactly **one** — the `AGENTS.md` form the create-via-REST channel appends unconditionally. It then declined to PATCH the body, correctly: `AGENTS.md` forbids re-sending a body that already carries an appended footer.

⇒ ⛔ Left as it is; a PATCH to satisfy a cosmetic preference is not worth breaking that rule for. ⚠️ But this is a **deviation from the order**, not a ruling: it does **not** establish option B of the earlier footer question (drop the dispatch footer), which this seat refused on authority — a standing instruction is not dropped by a dev omitting it. ⭐ It is, however, a **fourth data point** confirming row **A8** on #17710 exactly as corrected: #17714 one footer (no author footer), #17718 two, #17719 two, #17722 one. The append is the channel's; the doubling is the author's.

### Accepted as reported, ⛔ no card

- Both lists **re-derived by AST-parsing** rather than inherited — the 11 flags from `lint.ts`'s `static override flags` literal, the script maps from `init.ts`'s `TEMPLATES` plus the `create-objectstack` blank template's `package.json`. Four scaffolders, all declaring all three author-time scripts. The dev's readings agree with the card's **independently**, which is what makes the agreement worth something.
- ⭐ **Item ③ repaired as a CONDITION, not a list member** — the `--manifest-id` row now names the full three-step derivation chain, and a paragraph states that a derived id is held to `PackageSchema.manifestId` exactly as an explicit one is. That was the one way to fail this card while appearing to do it.
- ⚠️ **Four gates first answered NOT MEASURED rather than red**, and the dev read the **printed verdict** instead of the number — including `check:skill-examples`, which refused at **exit 1** with *"`packages/client-react/dist` holds no `.d.ts` declarations — the package is not built"*. ⭐ A prerequisite refusal wearing a finding's exit code is precisely why the verdict line is the reading and the status code is a field literal. One build under the lock cleared all four; re-run, all exit 0.
- The MDX compile was measured **with a control that shares the failure mode**: `@mdx-js/mdx` 3.1.1 compiles the edited page, and the same compiler on the same page **plus an unclosed `Callout`** is refused — so the green is a reading and not a no-op.
- `skip-changeset` verdict **measured, not assumed**: zero non-private packages name any content-shaped path in `files[]`, with `packages/spec`'s `files[]` read back as the control, and `apps/docs` (the only consumer) is `private: true`.
- The two `os init` / blank-template `build` script spellings (`objectstack compile` vs `objectstack build`) are **not** a defect — `os build` extends `Compile`, and `scaffold-ci-script-parity` records the divergence as deliberate. ⭐ Recorded because it reads like a defect on first inspection and a later reader might "fix" it.
- `Build Docs` **NOT MEASURED locally** and declared to CI — a 30-minute Next build over the foreground limit, which the deriver itself names as a path-scheduled CI job.

Landing follows once CI converges on `5d5f9ab0`; the review of record will carry the gate readings.

### ⭐ Item ① landed BROADER than the card asked, and correctly so

The card asked for three scripts named. The landed sentence reads:

> *"In a scaffolded project all three are wired as `npm run validate`, `npm run build` and `npm run lint` — the three `os init` templates (`app`, `plugin`, `empty`) and the `create-objectstack` blank template each declare all three sc…"*

⇒ it names the **four scaffolders explicitly**, which closes the "which scaffolder" ambiguity the original sentence left open. ⛔ Not scope creep: it is the same sentence, and the card's own history is that this sentence was under-inclusive for *different* scaffolders at different times (#16330 for the blank template, #16350 / PR #16888 for the `os init` maps). Naming them removes the axis the drift travelled on.

### ⚠️ A refinement to this seat's own A9 row, measured here

Row **A9** on #17710 states — on a single measurement from #17714 — that on a successful queue merge `removed_from_merge_queue` fires **one second before** `merged`. This landing measured them at the **same second**: both `20:18:29Z`.

⇒ the timing is not fixed and the row is being corrected to say so. ⛔ The load-bearing half is unaffected and still holds: on a successful merge **both** events appear, so `removed_from_merge_queue` alone is never evidence of an ejection — read it together with whether `merged` accompanies it.

### What landed

`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, the only authorised write surface — ⛔ zero `packages/spec/` paths, zero `content/docs/releases/` paths. `lint.ts`, `init.ts` and `publish.ts` were read as sources and **not edited**. Both lists derived by AST-parsing rather than hand-patched, and re-derived independently by this seat before the ACCEPT (review of record `5640043046`).

`Clause-②: no` · `skip-changeset`, the latter **measured** — zero non-private packages name a content-shaped path in `files[]`, with `packages/spec`'s `files[]` as the control, and the only consumer (`apps/docs`) is `private: true`.
